edition: Phaladeepika: V. Subrahmanya Sastri English translation, 1950, online OCR; Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra: Sanskrit and English transcription hosted by siva.sh, edition/translator not established by the displayed pages.
method: Retrieved chapter and verse texts with web search/open. Compared the proportional subperiod rule across two primary-text transcriptions. Exact anchors below are short locating excerpts, not a transcription of complete passages. No manuscript-critical edition or scan-image proofreading claim. Most lesson length consists of original conditional teaching, arithmetic, deliberately partial chart examples and exercises.

passages.exact_anchor: respectively declared the lords of the signs
passages.supported: Seven classical grahas own the twelve signs in the stated sequence; standard own/exaltation sign information. Used for sign-to-house arithmetic, not a full strength claim.
Nodes give effects according to conjunction with a bhava lord and the occupied bhava. Does not itself establish an unlimited dispositor chain; the lesson states that limitation explicitly.

passages.passage: Phaladeepika XV.18 and XV.25, lines 86–87 and 100
passages.exact_anchor: When any Bhava, its lord and its Karaka are all strong
passages.supported: Sign condition matters; bhava, its lord and karaka considered jointly. Used as a short general foundation, with the chain described as original teaching organization.

passages.exact_anchor: Some sages have expressed the view
passages.supported: Displayed text records more than one view of Rahu/Ketu own signs. Lesson therefore declares use of seven-graha sign rulership and does not silently mix nodal schemes.
General effects versus distinctive placement-based effects; strength conditions dasha interpretation. Original two-person comparison illustrates this distinction.

passages.exact_anchor: which is strong and which owns a certain Bhava
passages.supported: Chapter explicitly contrasts strength/weakness of house-owning planet in dasha interpretation. No deterministic promises drawn from later outcome lists.
Vimshottari years/order, first-period balance, and year convention. Lesson uses elapsed dasha-years rather than invented calendar dates; quarter-balance example is original arithmetic.
Mahadasha years times antardasha-lord years divided by 120; subperiod order begins with main lord. Full Jupiter timeline independently calculated.
Independent primary-text matching of the proportional subperiod formula.

search_intent.method: Searched primary-text keywords for Rahu association/dispositor, distinct dasha results, and bhukti calculation. These establish source relevance, not popularity, traffic, or search-volume claims.

distinct_from_existing.difference: Applied dispositor-chain calculation and stop rules, not introductory node disagreements or memorizing sign lords.
Controlled two-person lagna comparison, not only basic dasha definitions or a single yogakaraka case.
Expands original short contrast to a full subperiod timeline, balance-at-birth distinction, arithmetic and worked chart exercise.
